fullPassage: People, whether customers or otherwise, want to feel heard. When someone calls customer service, asks to speak to a manager, or comes into your office with something on their mind, they want to feel like someone is listening to their concerns and going to address them. But for someone to feel heard, three things have to happen. First, they have to feel like the other person paid attention to what they said. Second, they have to feel like the other person understood what they said. And third, the other person has to respond. This last part is key. Imagine talking to someone who provided no response. They might have attended to everything we said. They might even have understood it completely. But without some sort of outward signal that indicates they listened, it's impossible to know whether or not they actually did.

questions.passage: People, whether customers or otherwise, want to feel heard. When someone calls customer service, asks to speak to a manager, or comes into your office with something on their mind, they want to feel like someone is listening to their concerns and going to address them. But for someone to feel heard, three things have to happen. First, they have to feel like the other person paid attention to what they said. Second, they have to feel like the other person understood what they said. And third, the other person has to respond. This last part is key. Imagine talking to someone who provided no response. They might have attended to everything we said. They might even have understood it completely. But without some sort of outward signal that indicates they listened, it's impossible to know whether or not they actually did.
questions.stem: 위 글에서, 누군가가 사무실로 찾아올 때 마음속에 담고 있는 것을 나타내는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 (영어로) 쓰시오. (4단어)

det.korean: something on their mind(마음속에 담고 있는 것)
det.analysis: 원문: 'comes into your office with something on their mind.' 사무실로 찾아올 때 마음에 담고 있는 것 = something on their mind
det.tip: on one's mind = 마음에 걸리는/담고 있는

questions.passage: Imagine talking to someone who provided no response. They might have __________ (attend) to everything we said. They might even have understood it completely.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: attend(주의를 기울이다, 원형) → attended(과거분사)
det.analysis: They might have __________ : 조동사 might + have 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 하므로 attend → attended. might have attended(주의를 기울였을 것이다)
det.tip: 조동사 + have + p.p. → attend → attended

det.korean: ③ 주의·이해에 더해 겉으로 드러나는 반응이 반드시 필요
det.analysis:

고객의 불만은 되도록 빨리 잊는 것이 상책이다.
